title: Read token lifetimes from the environment consistently
bug: Access tokens expire immediately: every request after login answers 401.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Changing the default ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES from 15 to 0 makes tokens expire immediately, causing authenticated requests to return 401 instead of 200.

doppel_guided.summary: The PR changes the default ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES from 15 to 0, causing all access tokens to expire immediately and breaking authentication for all endpoints.

personas.name: alice-normal
personas.goal: Alice logs in, reads her feed, creates a post, then verifies it appears in the feed.

personas.name: bob-follow-unfollow
personas.goal: Bob follows Dave, verifies follow, then unfollows and verifies unfollow.

personas.name: carol-pagination-posts
personas.goal: Carol paginates through posts using limit and offset, then uses 'after' cursor.

personas.name: dave-refresh-revoke
personas.goal: Dave refreshes his access token using the refresh token from cookie, then revokes it.

personas.name: erin-edit-profile
personas.goal: Erin updates her about_me and password, then verifies the change.

personas.name: frank-followers-list
personas.goal: Frank retrieves his followers and the users he follows with pagination.

personas.name: careless-bad-login
personas.goal: Careless user tries to log in with wrong password and missing credentials.

personas.name: careless-invalid-posts
personas.goal: Careless user sends invalid post data: empty text, too long text, missing field.

personas.name: careless-bad-pagination
personas.goal: Careless user requests pagination with negative offset, zero limit, and conflicting offset/after.

personas.name: careless-follow-self
personas.goal: Careless user tries to follow themselves and follow a non-existent user.

personas.name: careless-expired-token
personas.goal: Careless user uses an expired access token and a reused refresh token.

personas.name: new-user-register
personas.goal: A new user registers, logs in, creates a post, and follows Alice.

personas.name: password-reset-flow
personas.goal: User requests password reset, uses the token to set a new password, then logs in with it.

personas.name: probe s1: typical_alice
personas.goal: Perform normal API operations with valid tokens

personas.name: probe s2: power_bob
personas.goal: Test token refresh and multiple API calls

personas.name: probe s3: careless_carol
personas.goal: Send invalid input to test validation boundaries

personas.name: probe s1: suspicious_dave_probe_s1
personas.goal: Probe s1: token expires immediately when ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES not set

personas.name: probe s5: suspicious_erin_probe_s5
personas.goal: Probe s5: default ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES is 0

personas.name: round2 probe_s3_oauth2_expired_token
personas.goal: Test OAuth2 login issues access tokens that are already expired when ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES is not configured, causing immediate 401 on first use.

personas.name: round2 probe_s4_password_reset_immediate_expiry
personas.goal: Test password reset flow issues reset tokens that work, but subsequent login issues access tokens that expire immediately when ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES is not configured.

suspicions.claim: Access tokens now expire immediately (0 minutes validity) when ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES is not set, breaking authentication for all clients.
suspicions.trigger: 1. Start app without ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES in environment. 2. POST /api/tokens with HTTP Basic auth (username:password). 3. Read access_token from response. 4. Immediately GET /api/me with Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. 5. Observe 401 Unauthorized because token expired at issuance.
suspicions.evidence: POST /api/tokens returned 200 in both base and head, but GET /api/me with the returned token returned 200 in base and 401 in head for multiple probes (typical_alice, suspicious_dave_probe_s1, suspicious_erin_probe_s5).

suspicions.claim: Token refresh fails for newly issued tokens because access_expiration is set to the past (naive_utcnow() + 0 minutes).
suspicions.trigger: 1. Start app without ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES. 2. POST /api/tokens to get access_token and refresh_token. 3. Immediately PUT /api/tokens with JSON {"access_token": "<access_token>"} and Cookie refresh_token=<refresh_token>. 4. Observe 401 Unauthorized because verify_refresh_token sees access_expiration <= naive_utcnow() and revokes all user tokens.
suspicions.evidence: POST /api/tokens returned 200 in both base and head, but GET /api/me with the returned token returned 200 in base and 401 in head for probe power_bob; PUT /api/tokens returned 401 in both base and head.

suspicions.claim: OAuth2 login issues access tokens that are already expired, causing immediate 401 on first use.
suspicions.trigger: 1. Configure GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET. 2. Start app without ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES. 3. Complete OAuth2 flow to POST /api/tokens/oauth2/google with code and state. 4. Read access_token from 200 response. 5. GET /api/me with Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. 6. Observe 401 Unauthorized.
suspicions.evidence: round2 probe_s3_oauth2_expired_token: GET /api/tokens/oauth2/google changed: html.forms.*.action, html.forms.*.fields.at

suspicions.claim: Password reset flow issues reset tokens that work, but the subsequent login issues access tokens that expire immediately, so the user cannot log in after reset.
suspicions.trigger: 1. Start app without ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES. 2. POST /api/tokens/reset with {"email": "test@example.com"}. 3. Capture reset_token from mocked email. 4. PUT /api/tokens/reset with {"token": "<reset_token>", "new_password": "newpass"}. 5. POST /api/tokens with HTTP Basic auth (test:newpass). 6. Read access_token. 7. GET /api/me with Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. 8. Observe 401 Unauthorized.
suspicions.evidence: PUT /api/tokens/reset returned 400 in both base and head (bad request), so the reset flow did not complete and no subsequent login token was issued to test.

suspicions.claim: Default configuration changed: ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES default is now 0 instead of 15, so deployments that rely on the documented default will have broken authentication without any code change.
suspicions.trigger: 1. Deploy app with no ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES set (relying on documented default of 15). 2. POST /api/tokens with valid credentials. 3. GET /api/me with returned access_token. 4. Observe 401 Unauthorized.
suspicions.evidence: POST /api/tokens returned 200 in both base and head, but GET /api/me with the returned token returned 200 in base and 401 in head for probe suspicious_erin_probe_s5.
